aboutTitle: A reference point for finding your direction.
aboutText: Polary takes its name from Polaris, the North Star: a reference for direction and constancy. We bring that idea to businesses by connecting the human side of a brand with the logic of data.
Founded by Gabriel Sales Camargo and Leonardo de Camargo Faria, Polary brings development and design together. Our mission is to turn complexity into clear, useful and efficient experiences.
values: Decisions grounded in context and intent.
Technology should make everyday work easier.
faq: We start with a conversation about your business, everyday challenges and what needs to change. That diagnosis helps us define priorities and scope.
Do I need all your solutions?
No. Our areas complement one another, but the solution depends on your needs. A project can start with a specific problem and evolve as the context changes.
Does Polary work on visual identity and websites?
Yes. Positioning, visual identity and digital presence are part of Polary’s documented work, connected to strategy and technology.
How do you use artificial intelligence?
We consider AI to support information organization, automation and analysis. Its use depends on a concrete need, the available data and a way to validate the benefit.
How much does a project cost, and how long does it take?
Cost and timing depend on scope, deliverables and integrations. We prepare a proposal after understanding your needs and defining the work.

casePageDescription: Diagnosis and a digital organization proposal for Paulo Ramos Barbearia: personal service, scheduling, management and data. A Polary final course project case study.
caseHero: Organize the routine. Preserve the care.
caseIntro: At Paulo Ramos Barbearia, personal service is part of the business. Polary’s proposal is to support that relationship with more organized operations.
caseSections: A business built on personal connection.

The interview describes a family learning tradition, service for different ages, reserved appointments according to individual needs and home visits when necessary. The barbershop also sells professional personal care products.

The documents record a lack of management software, predominantly manual processes and limited infrastructure. Without consolidated sales, scheduling and inventory records, it is harder to monitor operations and set priorities.

The proposal connects appointments, customers, services, products and financial information. The experience must stay simple and preserve human contact for people who find technology difficult to use.
Expected benefits, with criteria for measurement.

Less rework, clearer scheduling and better financial monitoring are goals of the proposal. The supplied materials contain no implementation measurements proving fewer missed appointments, higher revenue or improved productivity.
caseScope: Centralize appointments and records while respecting the preferences needed for service.
Organize records, sales and inventory movements.
Plan for expenses, salaries, cost centers and reports by date range.
Connect digital communication, user guidance, security and a backup strategy.
evidence: Operations rely on direct contact and manual records.
Actual system workflows and testing with the owner.
The project specifies scheduling, management and reporting as a proposal.
Deployment, stability and backend functional requirements.
There are opportunities to organize service and data.
A baseline and indicators for appointments, retention, sales and inventory.
sourcesText: The interview with Paulo, final course project documentation, strategic diagnoses, market research, planning and system requirements. Infrastructure proposals and market hypotheses are presented as proposals, not as deployment results.
